title: Delayed Impact of Fair Machine Learning
abstract: Static classification has been the predominant focus of the study of fairness in machine learning. While most models do not consider how decisions change populations over time, it is conventional wisdom that fairness criteria promote the long-term well-being of groups they aim to protect. This work studies the interaction of static fairness criteria with temporal indicators of well-being. We show a simple one-step feedback model in which common criteria do not generally promote improvement over time, and may in fact cause harm. Our results highlight the importance of temporal modeling in the evaluation of fairness criteria, suggesting a range of new challenges and trade-offs.

claims.text: Static fairness criteria (demographic parity and equal opportunity) do not generally promote long-term improvement in group mean score and can cause active harm.
Under the assumption that institution individual utility is more stringent than expected score changes, the optimal unconstrained utility policy (MaxUtil) never causes active harm.
Demographic parity and equal opportunity cause active harm to a protected group when applied over-eagerly in settings where the protected group proportion is small.
Equal opportunity can select at a lower rate than unconstrained utility maximization, causing relative harm to the protected group.
Systematic underestimation measurement error widens the regime in which fairness criteria yield favorable outcomes relative to unconstrained selection.
Directly maximizing expected group score change subject to institution utility loss constraints results in optimal threshold selection policies.

limitations.text: Prior study of fairness in machine learning focuses overwhelmingly on static classification without concern for temporal population impact.
The framework models decision impact over a single epoch and treats the effects on unselected individuals as zero-mean.
Direct outcome optimization relies heavily on the accuracy and availability of a two-variable causal outcome model.

future_work.text: Examine temporal impact characteristics beyond mean score changes, such as variance and individual-level outcomes.
Investigate outcome optimization strategies that are robust to modeling and measurement errors.

methodologies.name: One-step temporal feedback decision-making framework
methodologies.description: A mathematical framework modeling how static classification thresholds alter group score distributions over a single epoch through expected outcome functions.
datasets: 2003 TransUnion TransRisk FICO credit score sample
